identity.title: Rare Event Analysis of Large Language Models

problem.claim: The paper addresses systematic analysis of rare, highly significant LLM behaviors during inference.

gap.claim: Rare events are difficult to observe, and large-scale deployment can make behaviors unseen during development prominent.

contributions.claim: An end-to-end framework for analyzing rare events in LLMs.
A practical implementation covering theory, efficient generation, probability estimation, and error analysis.
Proposed extensions and applications to other models and contexts.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their contribution as an end-to-end, systematic framework spanning the listed analysis components.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report illustrating the implementation with concrete examples.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLM inference can produce atypical but consequential rare events.
Such events are hard to observe, while usage scale may amplify development-unseen behaviors in deployment.
The paper presents an end-to-end framework for systematic rare-event analysis.
The framework combines theory, generation, probability estimation, and error analysis, illustrated by examples.
The authors outline applications beyond the immediate model and context.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects rare-event analysis to deployment scale and presents a pipeline spanning generation, probability estimation, and error analysis.

lessons.interpretation: A rare-behavior study benefits from aligning its detection strategy with deployment-scale exposure and tracing uncertainty across the analysis pipeline.
lessons.application: Frame the evaluation around deployment-relevant event frequencies, then report how generation and probability-estimation errors affect identified cases.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when deployment scale or event probabilities cannot be meaningfully estimated.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the concrete examples, models, generation algorithms, probability estimators, error metrics, or quantitative results.
No comparative baselines or validation conditions are reported.
